# TCB Allowed List — Nanvix phys-mm

Any `external_body` outside this list must be removed.

## Allowed `external_body`

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::instance` — materializes a `&'static mut Inner` from the
  module-level `static mut INSTANCE: MaybeUninit<Inner>` singleton (guarded by `INSTANCE_INIT`).
  Raw-memory op over externally-owned `static mut` storage Verus cannot verify without a
  `PointsTo` (mirrors `bump_allocator`/`raw-array`). `ensures` pins the singleton's abstract
  state to `phys_view().frames`, asserts `(*r).inv()`, and records `phys_view().initialized` —
  the §8 ghost-token attachment for the singleton frame allocator.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::clear`
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` — materializes a
  `&'static mut [u8; N]` from a backend-provided address (`usize as *mut`); raw-memory
  op Verus cannot verify without a `PointsTo` for the externally-owned `BssStorage`
  region. Mirrors `src/libs/raw-array`. `ensures` states alignment + in-bounds over
  the abstract `bump_view`.
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc_as` — delegates to
  `alloc` and re-materializes the slot as `&'static mut MaybeUninit<T>`; same rationale.
  `ensures` adds the `size_of::<T>()`/`align_of::<T>()` vs `(N, A)` guard arms.

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`

- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::read` — reads a `TableEntry` from a
  page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *const E::Word`).
  Verus does not support `usize`→pointer casts (int-to-ptr materialization of externally-owned,
  volatile page-table memory), so the body cannot be verified. Same trust-boundary rationale as
  `bump_allocator::alloc` (`usize as *mut`) and `frame::instance`. See
  `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-table/verus-unsupported.md`. **The function is not contract-free:** it
  carries a full `#[verus_spec]` pinned to the global page-table-memory ghost — `requires index@ <
  PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@)` — exactly as
  `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` (parameter-free global ghost, no signature
  change).
- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::write` — writes a `TableEntry` into a
  page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *mut E::Word`).
  Same int-to-ptr / volatile externally-owned-memory limitation as `read`. Carries only the sound
  `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (auto from `TableIndex::inv`); it has **no** contents
  `ensures`. A contents postcondition pinning the *pure* global ghost `spec_table_word(self@.addr,
  index@)` to the caller-chosen `entry` would be unsound for an `external_body` (assumed)
  contract: two writes of distinct entries to the same slot would assume
  `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`, which with `lemma_entry_roundtrip` derives
  `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false` (Turn 2 review #2/#3/#15; exploit reproduced). The genuine `old@ -> @`
  slot-update transition (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)`, other slots framed) is therefore
  **deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token**, exactly the `identity_map_view()`
  `v -> v'` deferral convention in `identity_map.spec.rs`.

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging` (`mod.rs`)

- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/mod.rs::invlpg` — the body is a single
  `core::arch::asm!` block issuing the `invlpg` instruction, which flushes the CPU TLB
  entry for `vaddr`. Verus does not support inline-asm expressions, so the body cannot be
  verified — an external-bottom hardware trust boundary (same class as the volatile
  page-table access in `table::read`/`write` and the int-to-pointer materialization in
  `frame::instance`/`bump_allocator::alloc`). See
  `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-mod/verus-unsupported.md`. The effect is purely on hardware TLB
  state (outside Verus' memory model and invisible to every caller's Rust-visible state),
  so the faithful contract is **empty**: no `requires` (any `usize` is accepted), trivial
  `ensures` (returns `()`, no Rust-visible effect, every caller-side invariant preserved).
  This matches the inherited upstream
  `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.spec.rs:151`
  `pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::paging::invlpg ](vaddr: usize);` (no
  `requires`/`ensures`). No exec signature changed.

## Skip / exclude from current proof target

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::get_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::init`

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `mm::phys`

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_physical_memory_regions` — iterates an
  `alloc::collections::LinkedList` in a `for` loop. Verus has no `LinkedList` model and the
  orphan rule blocks providing one from the kernel crate (see
  `nanvix-phys-phys-mod/bugs.md`). Body cannot be verified; `ensures` states that, on `Ok`,
  every frame in `phys_regions_frame_set(&physical_memory_regions)` becomes reserved.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_mmio_regions` — same `LinkedList` limitation.
  `ensures` states that, on `Ok`, every *covered* frame in `mmio_regions_frame_set(mmio_regions)`

13. /// exec struct. Addresses use `int` (the `View` of `PhysicalAddress` / `PageAligned`), consistent

17.     /// page directory). Before initialization the boot page tables are still active and every
18.     /// `identity_map_page` is a successful no-op, so this flag selects which transition applies.
19.     pub initialized: bool,
20.

22.     /// address. Membership means: the page is **present, writable, supervisor-only**, and
23.     /// reachable at its own physical address in the kernel address space. Permissions are uniform
24.     /// across all mapped pages, so they are encoded by membership rather than stored per page.

44.     addr % spec_page_size() == 0

48. pub open spec fn spec_page_base(addr: int) -> int {
49.     addr - (addr % spec_page_size())
50. }
51. 
52. //==================================================================================================

54. //==================================================================================================
55. 
56. impl IdentityMapView {
57.     /// Implementation-consistency invariant (e.g. the abstract `mapped` set agrees with the

6. // Abstract state of the kernel identity map

9. /// Abstract state of the kernel identity map (see `view_design.md`).

11. /// This is a ghost model of *global* state: the in-scope functions are free functions backed by
12. /// the `KERNEL_PD_PADDR` / `KERNEL_CR3` atomics plus a BSS page-table pool, so there is no owning
13. /// exec struct. Addresses use `int` (the `View` of `PhysicalAddress` / `PageAligned`), consistent
14. /// with the sibling `mm::phys` abstraction (`FrameAllocView` keys frames by `int`).
15. pub ghost struct IdentityMapView {
16.     /// Whether the lazy identity mapper has been initialized (i.e. `init` has published the kernel
17.     /// page directory). Before initialization the boot page tables are still active and every
18.     /// `identity_map_page` is a successful no-op, so this flag selects which transition applies.
19.     pub initialized: bool,
20. 
21.     /// The set of identity-mapped pages, each identified by its page-aligned physical base
22.     /// address. Membership means: the page is **present, writable, supervisor-only**, and
23.     /// reachable at its own physical address in the kernel address space. Permissions are uniform
24.     /// across all mapped pages, so they are encoded by membership rather than stored per page.
25.     pub mapped: Set<int>,
26. }
27. 
28. /// Current abstract state of the global kernel identity map.
29. ///
30. /// Uninterpreted accessor: the identity-map state lives in module-level singletons

32. /// spec-readable. The cross-call transition (`v -> v'`) is realized in the proving phase by a
33. /// ghost token over those singletons; during the specification phase it is read like `self@`.
34. /// This mirrors `mm::phys::phys_view()` -- the same singleton-global boundary, not a verification
35. /// escape.
36. pub uninterp spec fn identity_map_view() -> IdentityMapView;
37.

39. // Page-address vocabulary
40. //==================================================================================================
41. 
42. /// An address is page-aligned when it is a multiple of the page size.
43. pub open spec fn spec_is_page_aligned(addr: int) -> bool {
44.     addr % spec_page_size() == 0
45. }
46. 
47. /// The page-aligned base address of the page containing `addr`.
48. pub open spec fn spec_page_base(addr: int) -> int {
49.     addr - (addr % spec_page_size())
50. }
51. 
52. //==================================================================================================
53. // Invariants and queries
54. //==================================================================================================
55. 
56. impl IdentityMapView {
57.     /// Implementation-consistency invariant (e.g. the abstract `mapped` set agrees with the
58.     /// present PDE/PTE bits and the page-table-pool bounds). Placeholder during specification;
59.     /// the proving phase fills it in once the concrete `view()` body is realized.

61.         true
62.     }

66.         &&& self.internal_inv()
67.         // Every recorded page is identified by a page-aligned base address.

69.         // Before initialization no lazy mapping has been installed; coverage is provided entirely
70.         // by the boot page tables.

72.     }

75.     /// boot tables make every page reachable; after init reachability is exactly membership in
76.     /// `mapped`. This is the headline resource callers obtain from `identity_map_page` on `Ok`.

4. //!
5. //! # Description
6. //!
7. //! This module implements identity mapping for physical memory accesses.
8. //!
9. //! Only the kernel process has physical memory identity-mapped into its virtual address space.
10. //! At boot, page tables are allocated from BSS for kernel code/data/bss/modules. During
11. //! [`init`], page tables for every PDE index in `[0, MEMORY_SIZE)` are pre-allocated from the
12. //! BSS pool, covering all physical memory. If a frame is later allocated outside these
13. //! pre-covered ranges, [`identity_map_page`] lazily installs a page table entry (and, when
14. //! necessary, a new page table from the BSS pool) for the corresponding PDE.
15. //!
16. //! When a new user address space is created, [`sync_kernel_pdes`] copies all present kernel
17. //! identity-mapping PDEs into the new page directory in a single pass.
18.

460. ///
461. /// # Notes
462. ///
463. /// If `size == 0`, this function is a no-op and returns success.
464. fn ensure_identity_mapped_range(
465.     start: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>,
466.     size: usize,
467. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
468.     debug_assert!(size.is_multiple_of(mem::PAGE_SIZE));
469. 
470.     if size == 0 {
471.         return Ok(());
472.     }
473. 
474.     let start_raw: usize = start.into_raw_value();
475.     let num_pages: usize = size / mem::PAGE_SIZE;
476.     for i in 0..num_pages {
477.         let page_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> =
478.             PageAligned::from_raw_value(start_raw + i * mem::PAGE_SIZE)?;
479.         identity_map_page(page_addr)?;
480.     }
481. 
482.     Ok(())
483. }
484. 
485. ///
486. /// # Description
487. ///
488. /// Ensures that a page table exists for the given PDE index in the kernel page directory. If the
489. /// PDE is already present, returns the physical address of the existing page table. Otherwise,
490. /// allocates a new page table from the BSS pool, installs the PDE, and returns the new page
491. /// table's physical address.
492. ///
493. /// # Parameters
494. ///
495. /// - `pd`: The kernel page directory table.
496. /// - `pde_idx`: The page directory index to check.
497. ///
498. /// # Returns
499. ///
500. /// Upon success, the physical address of the page table is returned. Upon failure, an error is
501. /// returned instead.
502. ///
503. /// # Errors
504. ///
505. /// - [`ErrorCode::InvalidArgument`]: Failed to read the PDE.
506. /// - [`ErrorCode::OutOfMemory`]: No BSS page table slots available.
507. /// - [`ErrorCode::BadAddress`]: The allocated page table frame number is out of range.
508. ///
509. #[verus_spec(result =>
510.     requires
511.         identity_map_view().inv(),
512.     ensures
513.         match result {
514.             // The returned page-table physical address is page-aligned (BSS-backed and
515.             // immediately usable as `Table::from_address` for the follow-up `ensure_pte`).
516.             // Ensuring a page table installs internal structure only -- it adds no page to the
517.             // identity map. The global map remains well-formed.
518.             Ok(pt_paddr) => {
519.                 &&& identity_map_view().inv()
520.                 &&& spec_is_page_aligned(pt_paddr as int)
521.             },
522.             // On failure no usable page-table address is produced and the identity map is left
523.             // well-formed: `ensure_pt` only ever installs *empty* page tables, so it maps no
524.             // page on either path (`mapped` is unaffected). A stronger `mapped`-equality
525.             // postcondition would require threading the pre-state (`old@`), but `ensure_pt`'s
526.             // signature is fixed -- its other caller `init` is out of scope and must not be
527.             // touched -- so invariant preservation is the strongest sound failure-state fact
528.             // expressible over the parameterless global view here. This is *not* `true`: it
529.             // guarantees a failed `ensure_pt` never corrupts the abstract identity map.
530.             Err(_) => identity_map_view().inv(),
531.         },
532. )]
533. fn ensure_pt(pd: Table<PageDirectoryEntry>, pde_idx: TableIndex) -> Result<usize, Error> {
534.     proof! { admit(); }
535.     let pde: PageDirectoryEntry = unsafe { pd.read(pde_idx) }.ok_or_else(|| {
536.         let reason: &str = "invalid PDE read from kernel PD";
537.         #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
538.         error!("ensure_pt(): {reason}");
539.         Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason)
540.     })?;
541. 
542.     if pde.is_present() {
543.         return Ok(pde.frame_address());
544.     }
545. 
546.     // No PT exists — allocate one from the BSS pool (zeroed = all PTEs absent).
547.     // SAFETY: atomic bump allocator ensures exclusive access to the slot;
548.     // BSS is zero-initialized, so assume_init_mut() is sound for integer arrays.
549.     let slot: &'static mut [PteWord; PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH] = unsafe {
550.         PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR
551.             .alloc_as::<[PteWord; PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH]>()
552.             .map_err(|e| {
553.                 #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
554.                 error!("ensure_pt(): page table allocation failed: {}", e);
555.                 Error::new(ErrorCode::OutOfMemory, "BSS page table allocation failed")
556.             })?
557.             .assume_init_mut()
558.     };
559.     let pt_paddr: usize = slot.as_ptr() as usize;
560. 
561.     // Install the PDE with type-safe flag constructors.
562.     let pt_frame: FrameNumber =
563.         FrameNumber::from_raw_value(pt_paddr / mem::PAGE_SIZE).ok_or_else(|| {
564.             let reason: &str = "BSS page table frame number out of range";
565.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
566.             error!("ensure_pt(): {reason}");
567.             Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, reason)
568.         })?;
569.     let new_pde: PageDirectoryEntry = PageDirectoryEntry::new(
570.         PageDirectoryEntryFlags::new(
571.             PresentFlag::Present,
572.             ReadWriteFlag::ReadWrite,
573.             UserSupervisorFlag::Supervisor,
574.             PageWriteThroughFlag::NotWriteThrough,
575.             PageCacheDisableFlag::CacheEnabled,
576.             AccessedFlag::NotAccessed,
577.             DirtyFlag::NotDirty,
578.             PageSizeFlag::Standard,
579.         ),
580.         pt_frame,
581.     );
582.     // SAFETY: the kernel PD is identity-mapped.
583.     unsafe { pd.write(pde_idx, new_pde) };
584. 
585.     Ok(pt_paddr)
586. }

610. #[verus_spec(result =>
611.     requires
612.         identity_map_view().inv(),
613.     ensures
614.         identity_map_view().inv(),
615.         match result {
616.             // The leaf step that realizes V==P: on success the page containing `phys_addr` is
617.             // present (writable, supervisor) and reachable at its own physical address. Membership
618.             // holds whether the PTE was freshly installed or already present (idempotent).
619.             Ok(_) => identity_map_view().mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr as int)),
620.             // On failure the leaf entry was not installed: the PTE was not already present (a
621.             // present PTE returns `Ok` via the idempotent fast path) and the read/frame-number
622.             // failure left it absent, so the page is *not* in the identity map. `identity_map_page`
623.             // propagates this and its caller must not treat the page as reachable.
624.             Err(_) => !identity_map_view().mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr as int)),
625.         },

634.         let reason: &str = "invalid PTE read from page table";

643. 
644.     // Fill the PTE with an identity mapping.
645.     let frame: FrameNumber =
646.         FrameNumber::from_raw_value(phys_addr / mem::PAGE_SIZE).ok_or_else(|| {
647.             let reason: &str = "frame number out of range";
648.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
649.             error!("ensure_pte(): {reason}");
650.             Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, reason)
651.         })?;
652.     let new_pte: PageTableEntry = PageTableEntry::new(
653.         PageTableEntryFlags::new(
654.             PresentFlag::Present,
655.             ReadWriteFlag::ReadWrite,
656.             UserSupervisorFlag::Supervisor,
657.             PageWriteThroughFlag::NotWriteThrough,
658.             PageCacheDisableFlag::CacheEnabled,
659.             AccessedFlag::NotAccessed,
660.             DirtyFlag::NotDirty,
661.         ),
662.         frame,
663.     );
664.     // SAFETY: the PT is identity-mapped.
665.     unsafe { pt.write(pte_idx, new_pte) };
666. 
667.     // Invalidate the TLB entry for this page.
668.     unsafe { paging::invlpg(phys_addr) };
669. 
670.     Ok(())
671. }

673. ///
674. /// # Description
675. ///
676. /// Identity-maps a single page in the kernel page directory.
677. ///
678. /// If the target PTE is already present, this function is a no-op. If the PDE is absent, a new
679. /// page table is allocated from the BSS pool and installed before the identity-mapped PTE is
680. /// created.
681. ///
682. /// # Parameters
683. ///
684. /// - `phys_addr`: Page-aligned physical address to identity-map.
685. ///
686. /// # Returns
687. ///
688. /// Upon success, empty is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
689. ///
690. /// # Errors
691. ///
692. /// - [`ErrorCode::InvalidArgument`]: Failed to read a valid paging entry.
693. ///
694. /// # Notes
695. ///
696. /// If the lazy mapper has not been initialized yet (boot page tables still active), this function
697. /// is a no-op and returns success.
698. #[verus_spec(result =>
699.     requires
700.         identity_map_view().inv(),
701.     ensures
702.         identity_map_view().inv(),
703.         match result {
704.             // The page containing `phys_addr` is reachable at its own physical address. After init
705.             // this means it is present (writable, supervisor) in the kernel page directory; before
706.             // init the call is a no-op and the boot page tables already cover it. Either way the
707.             // caller (`KernelFrame::new`) may subsequently read/write the frame through `phys_addr`.
708.             Ok(_) => identity_map_view().accessible(phys_addr@),
709.             // On failure the page was *not* made accessible, so `KernelFrame::new` must propagate
710.             // the error and must not dereference the frame. This is sound: an `Err` is only
711.             // reachable post-init (the pre-init path returns `Ok` as a no-op), and on the failure
712.             // path the page was not already mapped (an already-present PTE returns `Ok`) and the
713.             // failed `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte` did not map it -- so `accessible` is false. Mirrors
714.             // the `mm::phys` convention of stating the failure-state fact over the global view.
715.             Err(_) => !identity_map_view().accessible(phys_addr@),
716.         },
717. )]
718. pub(crate) fn identity_map_page(phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>) -> Result<(), Error> {
719.     proof! { admit(); }
720.     let phys_addr: usize = phys_addr.into_raw_value();
721. 
722.     let pd_paddr: usize = KERNEL_PD_PADDR.load(Ordering::Acquire);
723.     // Check if the lazy mapper has been initialized.
724.     if pd_paddr == 0 {
725.         return Ok(());
726.     }
727. 
728.     let pde_idx: TableIndex = paging::pd_index(phys_addr);
729.     let pte_idx: TableIndex = paging::pt_index(phys_addr);
730. 
731.     // SAFETY: the PD is identity-mapped.
732.     let pd: Table<PageDirectoryEntry> = unsafe { Table::from_address(pd_paddr) };
733.     let pt_paddr: usize = ensure_pt(pd, pde_idx)?;
734. 
735.     // SAFETY: the PT is identity-mapped (BSS-backed).
736.     let pt: Table<PageTableEntry> = unsafe { Table::from_address(pt_paddr) };
737.     ensure_pte(pt, pte_idx, phys_addr)
738. }

4. //!
5. //! # Description
6. //!
7. //! This module implements identity mapping for physical memory accesses.
8. //!
9. //! Only the kernel process has physical memory identity-mapped into its virtual address space.
10. //! At boot, page tables are allocated from BSS for kernel code/data/bss/modules. During
11. //! [`init`], page tables for every PDE index in `[0, MEMORY_SIZE)` are pre-allocated from the
12. //! BSS pool, covering all physical memory. If a frame is later allocated outside these
13. //! pre-covered ranges, [`identity_map_page`] lazily installs a page table entry (and, when
14. //! necessary, a new page table from the BSS pool) for the corresponding PDE.
15. //!
16. //! When a new user address space is created, [`sync_kernel_pdes`] copies all present kernel
17. //! identity-mapping PDEs into the new page directory in a single pass.
18.

98. ///
99. /// # Description
100. ///
101. /// Records the kernel page-directory and root paging-structure physical addresses used by the
102. /// lazy identity mapper.
103. ///
104. /// # Parameters
105. ///
106. /// - `kernel_pd_paddr`: Physical address of the kernel page directory.
107. /// - `kernel_cr3`: CR3 register value for the kernel root paging structure used for CR3 switching.
108. ///
109. /// # Returns
110. ///
111. /// Upon success, `Ok(())`. Upon failure, an error is returned and the global state remains
112. /// uninitialized (atomics are not published).
113. ///
114. /// # Notes
115. ///
116. /// On x86, `kernel_cr3` equals `kernel_pd_paddr` (the page directory is the CR3 root).
117. ///
118. /// This function pre-allocates a BSS page table for every PDE index in
119. /// `[0, MEMORY_SIZE)` that does not already have one. This covers all physical memory, so no
120. /// new PDEs are created at runtime. The kernel PD and CR3 atomics are published only after
121. /// pre-allocation succeeds, so other code never observes a partially-initialized identity map.
122. pub(crate) fn init(
123.     kernel_pd_paddr: PageDirectoryAddress,
124.     kernel_cr3: Cr3Register,
125. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
126.     // Pre-allocate page tables for all PDE indices in [0, MEMORY_SIZE).
127.     // This covers all physical memory, so no new PDEs are created at runtime.
128.     let pd_paddr: usize = kernel_pd_paddr.into_raw_value();
129.     let pde_count: usize = MEMORY_SIZE / mem::PGTAB_SIZE;
130.     for i in 0..pde_count {
131.         let pde_idx: TableIndex = paging::pd_index(i * mem::PGTAB_SIZE);
132.         // SAFETY: the PD is identity-mapped.
133.         let pd: Table<PageDirectoryEntry> = unsafe { Table::from_address(pd_paddr) };
134.         ensure_pt(pd, pde_idx)?;
135.     }
136. 
137.     // Publish the kernel PD and CR3 only after pre-allocation succeeds, so that other code
138.     // (e.g. `sync_kernel_pdes`, `with_kernel_address_space`) never observes a partially-
139.     // initialized identity map.
140.     KERNEL_PD_PADDR.store(kernel_pd_paddr.into_raw_value(), Ordering::Release);
141.     KERNEL_CR3.store(kernel_cr3.into_u32(), Ordering::Release);
142. 
143.     Ok(())
144. }

146. ///
147. /// # Description
148. ///
149. /// Copies bytes between two memory regions, after ensuring that both ranges are identity-mapped in
150. /// the kernel address space.
151. ///
152. /// # Parameters
153. ///
154. /// - `dst`: Destination physical address.
155. /// - `src`: Source physical address.
156. /// - `size`: Number of bytes to copy.
157. ///
158. /// # Returns
159. ///
160. /// Upon success, empty is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
161. ///
162. /// # Errors
163. ///
164. /// - [`ErrorCode::BadAddress`]: One of the physical ranges is invalid or overflows.
165. /// - Any error propagated by the lazy identity mapper while preparing the ranges.
166. ///
167. /// # Notes
168. ///
169. /// If `size == 0`, this function is a no-op and returns success.
170. ///
171. pub(crate) fn memcpy(dst: *mut u8, src: *const u8, size: usize) -> Result<(), Error> {
172.     // Check if copy size is zero.
173.     if size == 0 {
174.         return Ok(());
175.     }
176. 
177.     let dst_start: usize = dst as usize;
178.     let src_start: usize = src as usize;
179.     let dst_end: usize = dst_start.checked_add(size).ok_or_else(|| {
180.         error!("memcpy(): destination range overflows (dst={dst_start:#x}, size={size:#x})");
181.         Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, "memcpy(): destination range overflows")
182.     })?;
183.     let src_end: usize = src_start.checked_add(size).ok_or_else(|| {
184.         error!("memcpy(): source range overflows (src={src_start:#x}, size={size:#x})");
185.         Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, "memcpy(): source range overflows")
186.     })?;
187. 
188.     // Check if copy ranges overlap.
189.     if (dst_start..dst_end).contains(&src_start) || (src_start..src_end).contains(&dst_start) {
190.         error!(
191.             "memcpy(): source and destination ranges overlap (dst={dst_start:#x}, \
192.              src={src_start:#x}, size={size:#x})"
193.         );
194.         return Err(Error::new(
195.             ErrorCode::BadAddress,
196.             "memcpy(): source and destination ranges overlap",
197.         ));
198.     }
199. 
200.     with_kernel_address_space(|| {
201.         let src_addr: PhysicalAddress = PhysicalAddress::from_raw_value(src as usize)?;
202.         let (src_start, src_size) = page_aligned_cover(src_addr, size)?;
203.         ensure_identity_mapped_range(src_start, src_size)?;
204.         let dst_addr: PhysicalAddress = PhysicalAddress::from_raw_value(dst as usize)?;
205.         let (dst_start, dst_size) = page_aligned_cover(dst_addr, size)?;
206.         ensure_identity_mapped_range(dst_start, dst_size)?;
207. 
208.         // SAFETY: both `src` and `dst` are identity-mapped (virtual == physical) and
209.         // valid for `size` bytes. The overlap check above guarantees non-overlapping ranges.
210.         unsafe {
211.             fast_memcpy(dst, src, size);
212.         }
213.         Ok(())
214.     })
215. }

226. /// - `value`: Byte value to fill.

260.         // SAFETY: `base` is identity-mapped (virtual == physical) and valid for

269. ///
270. /// # Description
271. ///
272. /// Copies all present kernel identity-mapping PDEs from the kernel page directory into a target
273. /// page directory. This covers `[0, MEMORY_SIZE)` and ensures that the target PD (typically a
274. /// new user process PD) can access all kernel identity-mapped memory. Because all PDEs in this
275. /// range are pre-allocated at boot ([`init`]), this is a simple copy of already-present entries.
276. ///
277. /// # Parameters
278. ///
279. /// - `target_pd_paddr`: Physical address of the target page directory.
280. ///
281. /// # Returns
282. ///
283. /// Upon success, `Ok(())`. Upon failure, an error is returned.
284. ///
285. /// # Notes
286. ///
287. /// This function should be called once when constructing a new user address space.
288. ///
289. pub(crate) fn sync_kernel_pdes(target_pd_paddr: PageDirectoryAddress) -> Result<(), Error> {
290.     let kernel_pd_paddr: usize = KERNEL_PD_PADDR.load(Ordering::Acquire);
291.     if kernel_pd_paddr == 0 {
292.         return Ok(());
293.     }
294. 
295.     // SAFETY: the kernel PD is identity-mapped (BSS-backed). The target PD is backed by a
296.     // kernel page whose physical address is identity-mapped in the kernel address space.
297.     let kernel_pd: Table<PageDirectoryEntry> = unsafe { Table::from_address(kernel_pd_paddr) };
298.     let target_pd: Table<PageDirectoryEntry> =
299.         unsafe { Table::from_address(target_pd_paddr.into_raw_value()) };
300. 
301.     // Number of PDEs to sync — bounded by MEMORY_SIZE.
302.     let kernel_pde_count: usize = MEMORY_SIZE / mem::PGTAB_SIZE;
303. 
304.     for i in 0..kernel_pde_count {
305.         // SAFETY: `i` is always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH because MEMORY_SIZE < 4 GiB.
306.         let pde_idx: TableIndex = paging::pd_index(i * mem::PGTAB_SIZE);
307. 
308.         let kernel_pde: PageDirectoryEntry = unsafe { kernel_pd.read(pde_idx) }
309.             .ok_or_else(|| Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, "invalid PDE index"))?;
310. 
311.         if !kernel_pde.is_present() {
312.             continue;
313.         }
314. 
315.         // Only install the kernel PDE if the target PD does not already have one.
316.         let target_pde: PageDirectoryEntry = unsafe { target_pd.read(pde_idx) }
317.             .ok_or_else(|| Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, "invalid PDE index"))?;
318. 
319.         if !target_pde.is_present() {
320.             unsafe { target_pd.write(pde_idx, kernel_pde) };
321.         }
322.     }
323. 
324.     Ok(())
325. }

327. /// RAII guard that restores the original CR3 value when dropped.
328. struct Cr3Guard(Cr3Register);
329. 
330. impl Drop for Cr3Guard {
331.     ///
332.     /// # Description
333.     ///
334.     /// Restores the previously active CR3 value saved in this guard.
335.     ///
336.     fn drop(&mut self) {
337.         // SAFETY: caller runs at privilege level 0; CR3 holds a valid PD address.
338.         unsafe {
339.             self.0.write();
340.         }
341.     }
342. }
343. 
344. ///
345. /// # Description
346. ///
347. /// Temporarily switches CR3 to the kernel address space, executes `f`, and restores the previous
348. /// CR3 value on return.
349. ///
350. /// This gives `f` access to kernel identity mappings while preserving the caller's original
351. /// address-space context through RAII restoration.
352. ///
353. /// # Parameters
354. ///
355. /// - `f`: Closure to execute while CR3 points to the kernel address space.
356. ///
357. /// # Returns
358. ///
359. /// Returns the value produced by `f`.
360. ///
361. /// # Interrupt Safety
362. ///
363. /// The caller must ensure that interrupts are disabled or that interrupt handlers are
364. /// CR3-agnostic. If an interrupt fires while CR3 points to the kernel address space,
365. /// the handler will execute in the kernel address space rather than the original one.
366. ///
367. fn with_kernel_address_space<F, R>(f: F) -> R
368. where
369.     F: FnOnce() -> R,
370. {
371.     let kernel_cr3_raw: u32 = KERNEL_CR3.load(Ordering::Acquire);
372.     // Check if the kernel CR3 has been initialized.
373.     if kernel_cr3_raw == 0 {
374.         return f();
375.     }
376. 
377.     // SAFETY: caller runs at privilege level 0.
378.     let old_cr3: Cr3Register = unsafe { Cr3Register::read() };
379. 
380.     // If we are already in the kernel address space, no switch needed.
381.     // SAFETY: `kernel_cr3_raw` was produced by `Cr3Register::into_u32()` during `init()`,
382.     // so it is guaranteed to have no reserved bits set.
383.     let kernel_cr3: Cr3Register = unsafe { Cr3Register::from_u32_unchecked(kernel_cr3_raw) };
384.     if old_cr3 == kernel_cr3 {
385.         return f();
386.     }
387. 
388.     // Switch to kernel address space. The Cr3Guard restores `old_cr3` on drop.
389.     let _guard = Cr3Guard(old_cr3);
390.     // SAFETY: caller runs at privilege level 0; kernel_cr3 holds a valid PD address.
391.     unsafe {
392.         kernel_cr3.write();
393.     }
394. 
395.     f()
396. }

398. ///
399. /// # Description
400. ///
401. /// Computes the smallest page-aligned range that fully covers `[addr, addr + size)`.
402. ///
403. /// # Parameters
404. ///
405. /// - `addr`: Starting physical address of the target range.
406. /// - `size`: Number of bytes in the target range (must be > 0).
407. ///
408. /// # Returns
409. ///
410. /// Upon success, a tuple of the page-aligned start address and the page-aligned size is returned.
411. /// Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
412. ///
413. /// # Errors
414. ///
415. /// - [`ErrorCode::BadAddress`]: The range overflows or contains an invalid physical address.
416. ///
417. fn page_aligned_cover(
418.     addr: PhysicalAddress,
419.     size: usize,
420. ) -> Result<(PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>, usize), Error> {
421.     debug_assert!(size > 0);
422.     let start: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> =
423.         PageAligned::from_address(addr.align_down(PAGE_ALIGNMENT)?)?;
424.     // Compute the exclusive end as a raw `usize` rather than a `PhysicalAddress` because the
425.     // exclusive end may equal `MEMORY_SIZE`, which is out of bounds for `PhysicalAddress`.
426.     let raw: usize = addr.into_raw_value();
427.     let exclusive_end: usize = raw.checked_add(size).ok_or_else(|| {
428.         error!("page_aligned_cover(): physical range overflow (addr={raw:#x}, size={size:#x})");
429.         Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, "physical range overflow")
430.     })?;
431.     // Round exclusive end up to the next page boundary.
432.     let aligned_end: usize = exclusive_end
433.         .checked_next_multiple_of(mem::PAGE_SIZE)
434.         .ok_or_else(|| {
435.             error!("page_aligned_cover(): aligned end overflow (exclusive_end={exclusive_end:#x})");
436.             Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, "aligned end overflow")
437.         })?;
438.     let aligned_size: usize = aligned_end - start.into_raw_value();
439.     Ok((start, aligned_size))
440. }

442. ///
443. /// # Description
444. ///
445. /// Ensures that every page in `[start, start + size)` is identity-mapped in the kernel
446. /// page directory.
447. ///
448. /// # Parameters
449. ///
450. /// - `start`: Page-aligned starting physical address of the target range.
451. /// - `size`: Number of bytes in the target range (must be a multiple of [`PAGE_SIZE`]).
452. ///
453. /// # Returns
454. ///
455. /// Upon success, empty is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
456. ///
457. /// # Errors
458. ///
459. /// - [`ErrorCode::BadAddress`]: The range contains an invalid physical address.
460. ///
461. /// # Notes
462. ///
463. /// If `size == 0`, this function is a no-op and returns success.
464. fn ensure_identity_mapped_range(
465.     start: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>,
466.     size: usize,
467. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
468.     debug_assert!(size.is_multiple_of(mem::PAGE_SIZE));
469. 
470.     if size == 0 {
471.         return Ok(());
472.     }
473. 
474.     let start_raw: usize = start.into_raw_value();
475.     let num_pages: usize = size / mem::PAGE_SIZE;
476.     for i in 0..num_pages {
477.         let page_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> =
478.             PageAligned::from_raw_value(start_raw + i * mem::PAGE_SIZE)?;
479.         identity_map_page(page_addr)?;
480.     }
481. 
482.     Ok(())
483. }

485. ///
486. /// # Description
487. ///
488. /// Ensures that a page table exists for the given PDE index in the kernel page directory. If the
489. /// PDE is already present, returns the physical address of the existing page table. Otherwise,
490. /// allocates a new page table from the BSS pool, installs the PDE, and returns the new page
491. /// table's physical address.
492. ///
493. /// # Parameters
494. ///
495. /// - `pd`: The kernel page directory table.
496. /// - `pde_idx`: The page directory index to check.
497. ///
498. /// # Returns
499. ///
500. /// Upon success, the physical address of the page table is returned. Upon failure, an error is
501. /// returned instead.
502. ///
503. /// # Errors
504. ///
505. /// - [`ErrorCode::InvalidArgument`]: Failed to read the PDE.
506. /// - [`ErrorCode::OutOfMemory`]: No BSS page table slots available.
507. /// - [`ErrorCode::BadAddress`]: The allocated page table frame number is out of range.
508. ///
509. #[verus_spec(result =>
510.     requires
511.         identity_map_view().inv(),
512.     ensures

1. # View Design: `mm::virt::identity_map`
2. 
3. ## Abstract Resource
4. 
5. To callers, this module is the **kernel's identity map**: a single global,
6. write-and-supervisor mapping that answers one question — *"is this physical page
7. reachable at its own physical address (V == P) in the kernel address space?"* —
8. and, when asked, makes it so without consuming frame-allocator memory.
9. 
10. It is a process-wide **singleton** (backed by the `KERNEL_PD_PADDR` / `KERNEL_CR3`
11. statics plus a BSS page-table pool). The in-scope functions are free functions,
12. not methods on an exec struct, so the View models the *global* identity-map state
13. rather than the contents of any one passed-in `Table`. How that global ghost
14. state is threaded (ghost global vs. tracked token) is a specification-phase
15. concern; this document fixes only the abstraction.
16. 
17. ## View Struct
18. 
19. ```rust
20. /// Abstract state of the kernel identity map.
21. ///
22. /// This is a ghost model of global state — there is no owning exec struct.
23. pub struct IdentityMapView {
24.     /// Whether the lazy identity mapper has been initialized (i.e. `init` has
25.     /// published the kernel page directory). Before initialization the boot
26.     /// page tables are still active and every `identity_map_page` is a
27.     /// successful no-op, so this flag selects which transition applies.
28.     pub initialized: bool,
29. 
30.     /// The set of identity-mapped pages, each identified by its page-aligned
31.     /// physical base address. Membership means: the page is **present,
32.     /// writable, supervisor-only**, and reachable at its own physical address
33.     /// in the kernel address space. Permissions are uniform across all mapped
34.     /// pages, so they are encoded by membership rather than stored per page.
35.     ///
36.     /// Implementation note: realized as `Set<int>` (not `Set<usize>`) in
37.     /// `identity_map.spec.rs`, because `PhysicalAddress@` and
38.     /// `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>@` both view as `int`. This keeps
39.     /// `mapped.contains(phys_addr@)` and `spec_page_base(..)` typechecking
40.     /// directly and matches `FrameAllocView`'s address element type.
41.     pub mapped: Set<int>,,
42. }
43. ```
44. 
45. ### Spec functions (signatures designed here; bodies are spec-phase work)
46. 
47. ```rust
48. impl /* global identity map */ {
49.     /// Maps concrete (global) state to the abstract identity map.
50.     /// Public so callers can name the abstract state; closed so the mapping
51.     /// from `KERNEL_PD_PADDR`, the page directory, and the page-table pool
52.     /// does not leak.
53.     pub closed spec fn view(/* ghost global */) -> IdentityMapView;
54. }
55. 
56. impl IdentityMapView {
57.     /// Implementation-consistency invariant (e.g. the abstract `mapped` set
58.     /// agrees with the present PDE/PTE bits, page-table pool bounds, etc.).
59.     /// Cannot be written until implementation bodies are visible — left as a
60.     /// placeholder; the specification phase fills it in.
61.     pub closed spec fn internal_inv(self) -> bool {
62.         true
63.     }
64. }
65. ```
66. 
67. ## Well-formedness Invariant
68. 
69. ```rust
70. impl IdentityMapView {
71.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
72.         &&& self.internal_inv()
73.         // Every recorded page is identified by a page-aligned base address.
74.         &&& (forall|p: usize| self.mapped.contains(p) ==> is_page_aligned(p))
75.         // Before initialization no lazy mapping has been installed; coverage
76.         // is provided entirely by the boot page tables.
77.         &&& (!self.initialized ==> self.mapped =~= Set::empty())
78.     }
79. }
80. ```
81. 
82. `is_page_aligned(p) := p % PAGE_SIZE == 0` is a free spec helper (constant
83. resolved in the spec phase). Both conjuncts are abstraction-level truths any
84. implementation maintains, not statements about a particular layout.
85. 
86. Monotonicity ("a mapped page is never unmapped or remapped") is a property of
87. *transitions*, so it lives in `ensures` (e.g. `old@.mapped.subset_of(self@.mapped)`),
88. not in `inv()`.
89. 
90. ## Spec Transition / Query Functions
91. 
92. ```rust
93. impl IdentityMapView {
94.     /// Page is reachable at its own physical address right now.
95.     /// Before init, the boot tables make every page reachable; after init,
96.     /// reachability is exactly membership in `mapped`. This is the headline
97.     /// resource callers obtain from `identity_map_page` on `Ok`.
98.     pub open spec fn accessible(self, page: usize) -> bool {
99.         !self.initialized || self.mapped.contains(page)
100.     }
101. 
102.     /// Unconditional install of one page (idempotent). Models the leaf step
103.     /// `ensure_pte` realizes: it always adds the page to the map.
104.     pub open spec fn spec_install_page(self, page: usize) -> IdentityMapView {
105.         IdentityMapView { mapped: self.mapped.insert(page), ..self }
106.     }
107. 
108.     /// Full effect of `identity_map_page`: install the page when the mapper is
109.     /// initialized, otherwise a no-op (boot tables already cover it). Either
110.     /// way the page ends up `accessible`.
111.     pub open spec fn spec_map_page(self, page: usize) -> IdentityMapView {
112.         if self.initialized {
113.             self.spec_install_page(page)
114.         } else {
115.             self
116.         }
117.     }
118. }
119. ```
120. 
121. ### How each in-scope function uses the View
122. 
123. | Function | View-level effect | Notes |
124. |----------|-------------------|-------|
125. | `identity_map_page(phys_addr)` | `self@ == old@.spec_map_page(base(phys_addr@))`; on `Ok`, `self@.accessible(base(phys_addr@))` | `base(a) := align_down(a, PAGE_SIZE)`; equals `a` for the page-aligned input. On `Err`, `self@ == old@` and the page need not be accessible. |
126. | `ensure_pte(pt, pte_idx, phys_addr)` | `self@ == old@.spec_install_page(base(phys_addr))` (idempotent) | The leaf step that realizes V==P; `identity_map_page` wraps it with the `initialized` guard. |
127. | `ensure_pt(pd, pde_idx)` | `self@.mapped == old@.mapped` (identity at the page abstraction) | Allocating/installing a page table establishes *internal structure* only — its PTEs start absent, so no page becomes mapped. Returns an opaque page-aligned `pt_paddr`. Idempotent: a present PDE leaves state unchanged. Also called by `init` to pre-allocate. |
128. 
129. The two private helpers deliberately have **no PDE/PTE-index fields in the
130. View**: the caller analysis states callers "don't care about the page-directory /
131. page-table index split." `ensure_pt` contributes nothing to `mapped`; only
132. `ensure_pte` does. Their composition inside `identity_map_page` is exactly
133. `spec_map_page`.
134. 
135. ## Design Rationale
136. 
137. **`initialized: bool`** — The contract has a genuine pre-init mode: before `init`
138. publishes the kernel PD, `identity_map_page` succeeds as a no-op and the page is
139. reachable through boot tables. This flag is the minimal abstract state needed to
140. state that conditional transition (`spec_map_page`) and to make `accessible`
141. total. *Substitution test:* any lazy-mapper implementation has a "not yet set up,
142. boot tables cover memory" phase versus an "active" phase; the flag survives a
143. rewrite. It is never a stand-in for the concrete `KERNEL_PD_PADDR == 0` check —
144. callers observe a *mode*, not an atomic.
145. 
146. **`mapped: Set<usize>`** — The core resource: which physical pages are
147. identity-mapped (present + writable + supervisor). Callers reason purely in terms
148. of set membership ("is my frame reachable?"), and idempotence/monotonicity are
149. naturally `insert` / `subset_of` on a `Set`. *Substitution test:* every possible
150. implementation — two-level x86 tables, a flat array, a different paging scheme —
151. must track *which pages are mapped*; the set is implementation-agnostic. Elements
152. are page-aligned base addresses (`usize`) because callers already hold
153. `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>` and the skill keeps addresses as `usize`; this
154. avoids introducing division/frame-number arithmetic at the abstraction surface.
155. 
156. **Permissions encoded by membership, not a field** — These functions only ever
157. create writable, supervisor mappings, so per-page permission state would be a
158. constant. Folding "writable + supervisor" into the meaning of `mapped`
159. membership keeps the View minimal while still letting `KernelFrame::clear` /
160. `memset` rely on writability.
161. 
162. **`accessible` as a derived query** — Gives callers a single predicate for the
163. postcondition they actually want ("the frame is reachable now") that is uniform
164. across the pre-init and post-init cases, so caller proofs don't branch on
165. `initialized`.
166. 
167. **`inv()` conjuncts** — `is_page_aligned` over `mapped` is the abstraction's
168. well-formedness (a "page" is a page-aligned unit). The `!initialized ==> mapped
169. empty` conjunct is the cross-field consistency that justifies `spec_map_page`'s
170. no-op branch (nothing is silently dropped when not initialized). Both are
171. caller-visible truths and hold for any implementation.
172. 
173. **Field usage (minimality check)** — `initialized` is used in `spec_map_page`,
174. `accessible`, and `inv`; `mapped` is used in every spec function. No field is
175. dead.
176. 
177. | Criterion | Result |
178. |-----------|--------|
179. | Substitution | ✅ both fields survive a full rewrite |
180. | Caller-only | ✅ no PDE/PTE indices, flag bits, BSS-pool, or CR3 mechanics leak |
181. | Complete | ✅ accessibility, idempotence, monotonicity, pre-init no-op all expressible |
182. | Minimal | ✅ two fields, both referenced by specs |
183. | No code-as-spec | ✅ describes *which pages are mapped*, not *how* |
184. 
185. ## Rejected Alternatives
186. 
187. - **Two-level `Map<TableIndex, Map<TableIndex, usize>>` (PD → PT → frame).**
188.   Mirrors the x86 page-table structure and the `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte` split.
189.   Rejected: the caller analysis explicitly says external callers don't care about
190.   the PD/PT index split or `Table::from_address` mechanics — this is an
191.   abstraction leak (Over-Faithful anti-pattern). The page-granular `Set` captures
192.   everything callers observe.
193. 
194. - **`mapped: Set<nat>` keyed by frame number (`addr / PAGE_SIZE`).** Equivalent
195.   power, but forces division semantics into the abstraction and diverges from the
196.   `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>` (a `usize`) callers actually pass. Page-aligned
197.   `usize` base addresses are more directly usable in caller specs.
198. 
199. - **Per-page permission/flags field (e.g. `Map<usize, Perms>`).** All mappings
200.   are uniformly writable + supervisor, so this would store a constant. Encoded by
201.   `mapped` membership instead.
202. 
203. - **A `pt_pool_used: nat` / remaining-BSS-slots field.** Callers explicitly don't
204.   care about page-table-pool bookkeeping; `OutOfMemory` is observed only as an
205.   `Err`. Exhaustion is a failure outcome, not abstract state callers reason about.
206.   Belongs (if anywhere) inside `internal_inv()`, not the public View.
207. 
208. - **`kernel_pd_paddr: usize` / `cr3` fields.** These are concrete handles to the
209.   paging structures, not caller-observable abstract state. Callers never name the
210.   kernel PD address; replacing it (or the CR3 root) with a different mechanism
211.   must not change the spec. Leaking them fails the substitution test.
212. 
213. - **A separate per-`Table` View for `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`.** Tempting because
214.   they take a `Table` argument, but they are private sub-steps of a single global
215.   operation; giving them independent View types would fragment the abstraction and
216.   re-expose the index structure. They are specified as refinements of
217.   `spec_install_page` / the identity transition on the one global
218.   `IdentityMapView`.
219. 
220. - **No `initialized` flag (treat init as just another mapping).** Then
221.   `identity_map_page`'s pre-init no-op success could not be stated precisely, and
222.   `accessible` would wrongly require `mapped` membership during early boot. The
223.   flag is the minimal addition that captures the documented pre-init transparency.
224.

data.reasoningText:
I'm checking whether the `identity_map_page` implementation satisfies the caller's expectations. The first requirement—that the page is present and identity-mapped with readable and writable access through the physical address—appears to be covered by the `accessible` predicate, though it's worth noting that this encodes both mapped and pre-initialized states. The second requirement around idempotence and safe no-op behavior is built into the spec through how `spec_install_page` handles insertions, but the thought cuts off before fully confirming this.

Looking at the remaining expectations: supervisor and read-write permissions are documented in the View's membership semantics rather than as explicit predicates in the ensures clause, which is a documentation-level abstraction but not formally checkable. TLB consistency isn't captured in the spec at all since `invlpg` has an empty contract—this is a hardware effect outside Verus's memory model. The pre-initialization no-op case is covered by how `accessible` behaves when uninitialized. However, there's a significant gap: the caller expects no recursion into frame allocation, but the View has no notion of the frame allocator, so this structural property isn't expressible in the current contract.

For the error case, the ensures clause correctly captures that the frame is inaccessible on failure. Moving to `ensure_pt`, the spec covers page alignment and invariant preservation, but the caller also expects the PDE to be present afterward and `pt_paddr` to be the page table's frame address—neither of which is explicitly expressed. The error arm only preserves the invariant, which is acknowledged as the strongest expressible but remains a weak guarantee.

The critical issue is that all three functions are `admit()`-ed, so none of these ensures are actually proven—they're just claims. This means caller coverage at the spec level is partial and proof coverage is zero. Examining spec quality more closely: the ensures clauses aren't tautological since `inv()` contains real constraints like alignment and pre-initialization emptiness, though `internal_inv()` is just a placeholder `true`. This reveals a fundamental weakness: since `internal_inv` is trivially true and `identity_map_view()` is uninterpreted, the abstract `mapped` set is completely disconnected from the concrete page table state.

The entire verification is vacuous—an uninterpreted view combined with `internal_inv=true` and `admit()` bodies means nothing is actually proven. two compounding facts:

- `identity_map_view()` is `uninterp` (spec.rs:36) AND `IdentityMapView::internal_inv()` is the
  literal placeholder `true` (spec.rs:60-62). The implementation-consistency invariant that is
  supposed to tie the abstract `mapped` set to the real PDE/PTE present-bits is therefore *not
  encoded at all*. The View is completely disconnected from the concrete page tables.
- The three exec bodies are entirely `admit()`-ed (see below), so none of the ensures are
  proven against the code.

Detailed criteria:
- **No tautological ensures:** mostly OK. `ensure_pt`'s `Err(_) => identity_map_view().inv()`
  (spec.rs:530) is not literally `true` (inv() carries the alignment + pre-init-empty
  constraints), but it is a *weak* failure postcondition — it says nothing about `mapped`.
  `ensure_pte`'s `Err(_) => !mapped.contains(page_base)` (rs:624) and `identity_map_page`'s
  `Err(_) => !accessible(phys_addr@)` (rs:715) are genuinely meaningful, non-tautological
  error paths. Good.
- **Mathematical types:** addresses modeled as `int`, `mapped: Set<int>` — appropriate.
- **inv() encodes real constraints:** partial. The two outer conjuncts (alignment of every
  mapped page; `!initialized ==> mapped == empty`) are real. But `internal_inv() == true`
  removes the *only* invariant that would make the spec non-trivial, so `inv()` does not
  constrain the abstract state to match reality.
- **Subsumption:** on `identity_map_page` Ok, `accessible(phys_addr@)` is trivially `true`
  whenever `!initialized` (accessible returns `!initialized || ...`). That is intended no-op
  semantics, acceptable.
- **Permissions / TLB:** the "writable, supervisor" and "TLB-consistent" guarantees callers
  rely on are only *documentation* (View doc-comments at spec.rs:22-25), not checkable
  predicates. invlpg carries an empty contract, so TLB consistency is not expressed in spec.

consistent — but they only relate `spec_install_page`/`spec_map_page` to each other; they never
touch the exec bodies, which are admitted.

  explicit predicate.

  structural guarantee; the View has no frame-allocator notion.

tcb-allowed.md entry here. The dependencies the bodies lean on (`Table::read`/`write`,

already listed in tcb-allowed.md. The three in-scope functions are correctly NOT marked
external_body — but they substitute `admit()` instead, which is worse (zero proof, and not even
a recorded trust boundary). Compliant on the letter of the TCB list; defeated by admit().

   and `internal_inv() == true`, so the abstract `mapped`/`accessible` model is never tied to

   actual page-table state.

   (b) TLB consistency, (c) explicit writable/supervisor permission; `ensure_pt` Ok omits
   "PDE present / pt_paddr is the PT frame address."

## Result: FAIL
